summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (L6) proposing that after senescent-cell/SASP clearance lowers CD38 load, a residual NAD-precursor pulse (NMN/NR class) raises tissue NAD more than a matched CD38-inhibitor pulse at the same post-clearance timepoint. The claim is a direct flip of the competing L5 hypothesis; both are mutually exclusive predictions on the same unperformed head-to-head assay. No experimental data has been generated; the card is entirely based on literature synthesis and a proposed assay design.

content_blocks.title: Central Claim (L6 Hypothesis)
content_blocks.content: After documented senescent-cell/SASP clearance lowers CD38 load, a residual NAD-precursor pulse (NMN/NR class) raises tissue NAD more than a matched CD38-inhibitor pulse at the same post-clearance timepoint. Pre-registered threshold: ΔNAD_precursor − ΔNAD_CD38i ≥ 20% of the larger arm (or precursor wins on a pre-registered superiority test). This is the direct flip of L5, which claimed CD38i > precursor in the same post-clearance residual ranking. L5 and L6 are mutually exclusive predictions on one unperformed assay.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Subtract-before-add strategy: clear SASP-driven CD38+ macrophage load first, then pulse leftover levers. CD38 gates age-related NAD decline and NMN degradation; senescent/SASP ablation lowers CD38 and partially restores NAD; ecto-CD38 block raises NAD via an NMN-dependent route; 78c-class CD38i improves aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy (not a post-senolysis factorial). Flip motivation: after CD38↓, the residual CD38i target shrinks; because ecto-block is NMN-dependent, residual precursor can regain the larger ΔNAD once CD38 load is already low — opposite ranking to L5.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Evidence
content_blocks.content:
Four key literature references underpin the mechanistic rationale:
1. PMID 27304511 (Camacho-Pereira 2016, Cell Metab, DOI 10.1016/j.cmet.2016.05.006, PMC4911708): Age-related NAD↓ requires CD38; CD38 is the major in vivo NMN-degrading activity.
2. PMID 33199924 (Covarrubias 2020, Nat Metab, DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00305-3, PMC7908681): SASP induces CD38-high macrophages that reduce tissue NAD.
3. PMID 33199925 (Chini 2020, Nat Metab, DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00298-z, PMC8752031): Senescent/SASP ablation ↓CD38 and partially restores NAD; ecto-CD38 block raises NAD NMN-dependently.
4. PMID 35263032 (Tarragó 2022, Aging Cell, DOI 10.1111/acel.13589, PMC9009115): CD38i 78c improves median survival/healthspan (~10% median survival increase class effect) in aged mice as monotherapy — not a post-senolysis residual ranking study.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed and Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: After senolysis, residual CD38 inhibition always beats residual NAD precursor (L5 seed), or stacking both is always better than ranking which residual lever wins.
Baseline measured:
- CD38 gates age NAD/NMN fate: LITERATURE (PMID 27304511)
- SASP→CD38+ macrophages→tissue NAD↓: LITERATURE (PMID 33199924)
- Clearance ↓CD38 + partial NAD rebound; ecto-block NMN-dependent: LITERATURE (PMID 33199925)
- 78c aged-mouse benefit: LITERATURE monotherapy (PMID 35263032)
- Post-clearance H2H residual ΔNAD precursor vs CD38i: UNKNOWN (PubMed soft-complete 0)
- Residual ranking margin ≥20%: PREDICTION (flip of L5)
- L5 does not already prove this flip — same missing assay; rankings mutually exclusive.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat L5 as proving L6 — L5 left H2H UNKNOWN and only listed this flip as a competing PREDICTION; one 2-arm residual pulse decides both cards.
2. Incomplete clearance: residual CD38+ macrophages can still favor CD38i even after partial senolysis — flip is not automatic from 'CD38 fell.'
3. 78c monotherapy ≠ residual after subtract — aged-mouse survival does not rank post-senolysis residual arms.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Method and Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Method: propose-assay. Design: Pre-registered aged tissue or SASP-conditioned system; senolytic/SASP-ablation run-in → wash → 2-arm residual pulse (NMN/NR vs CD38i). Tissue targets: WAT/liver. Verification: CD38 activity + SC/SASP marker at post-clearance sampling. Refute if: On the pre-registered post-clearance panel, residual CD38i ΔNAD ≥ residual precursor ΔNAD (or the ≥20% precursor-superiority margin fails) when CD38↓ is verified — especially under incomplete clearance where residual CD38+ load remains high and L5 ranking can still win.

key_findings: No experiments have been run (execution_status=NOT_RUN); the entire card is a hypothesis/proposed assay at TRL 1.

Central claim (L6): after senescent-cell/SASP clearance lowers CD38 load, residual NMN/NR-class precursor pulse raises tissue NAD more than a matched CD38-inhibitor pulse (ΔNAD_precursor − ΔNAD_CD38i ≥ 20% of the larger arm).
This is the direct flip of L5 hypothesis; both L5 and L6 are mutually exclusive predictions on the same unperformed head-to-head post-clearance assay.
Post-clearance H2H residual NAD ranking (precursor vs CD38i) is explicitly UNKNOWN — PubMed soft-complete 0; no dedicated assay found in literature.

Four supporting literature references establish mechanistic plausibility: CD38 as major NMN-degrading activity (PMID 27304511), SASP-induced CD38-high macrophages reducing tissue NAD (PMID 33199924), senolysis lowering CD38 with partial NAD rebound and NMN-dependent ecto-block (PMID 33199925), and 78c CD38i improving aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy (PMID 35263032).
78c monotherapy aged-mouse survival benefit (~10% median survival increase) does not constitute evidence for post-senolysis residual arm ranking.
Key risk: incomplete clearance leaves residual CD38+ macrophages that could still favor CD38i, meaning the flip is not automatic from a partial CD38 reduction.
Time to refute estimated at 6 weeks; kill cost tier 2; IP class: subtract-before-add; FTO status UNKNOWN.
No sequences, analog lists, unpublished constructs, or proprietary molecular keys are disclosed.
